transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in?

I'm just... having trouble keeping my mind on things. At the warehouse, every little thing pulls me away. A beeper, a forklift, someone moving a pallet... I lose track of the count. Then I realize I've put the wrong numbers in the inventory.
When did you first start noticing these problems with concentration—have they been present since you were a kid, or is this something that started more recently?

Um... no, not since I was a kid. It's... it's just been the last month or so. My husband stopped working outside the house recently, and... I guess our routine just changed. That's when I started noticing it.
Since your husband's routine changed about a month ago, have you been feeling down, sad, or noticing that you've lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
No... not really. I wouldn't say I feel sad. I still do my normal things, mostly. It's just... having a hard time focusing at work, like I said.

Besides your concentration at work, have you noticed yourself worrying a lot, more than you think you should, about various things in your life—like health, family, or finances—even when there's no clear reason to worry?
No... I don't think so. Just the normal amount, I guess. I'm not really sitting around worrying about things... it's just the focus at the warehouse.

Can you tell me more about how you've been feeling emotionally since your husband stopped working outside the home—do you find yourself feeling stressed, overwhelmed, or unsettled by the change in your routine?

Um... I wouldn't say stressed. Some days I actually feel... almost too upbeat, I guess. Like I could fix up the whole house and get everything done at the warehouse before dinner. But... well, if my husband questions one of my plans while I'm trying to do all that, I... I guess I've been snapping at him over little things. It's just... adjusting to him being around so much, probably.
When you have those upbeat, high-energy days, how many days in a row does that feeling usually last?
I don't really count the days... it's just, well, this whole thing has been going on for about a month now. Ever since he stopped working outside the house and our routine changed.
During those days when you feel unusually upbeat and energetic, have you noticed that you need less sleep than usual but still feel rested and full of energy?
I haven't really... I don't know. I guess I've been sleeping fine. I haven't noticed anything different with my sleep.
During those upbeat, high-energy days, have you noticed your thoughts racing or jumping quickly from one idea to another, or that you're talking more than usual?

I mean... I guess people have said something. My husband... and some of the guys at the warehouse. They say I talk too fast. Um... about recipes I want to try, or... new safety ideas for the floor, or art classes. They say they can't get a word in edge-wise. But... I just feel like if I don't get it all out right then, the thought is just gonna... disappear. So I have to finish it.

During these upbeat, high-energy periods, has it caused any serious problems—like conflicts with coworkers, trouble at work, or other consequences—or has it mostly just been noticeable without really disrupting your daily life?

I guess... it's caused some issues. I've made a few mistakes with the inventory at work, so I have to keep double-checking things with my supervisor. And... well, at home, my husband and I have been arguing a lot more. It's just... instead of enjoying his retirement, it feels like we're just walking around each other to avoid a fight.

Have you ever had a period in the past—lasting a week or more—where you felt unusually depressed, low, or lost interest in things, or another time where you felt extremely high-energy or 'on top of the world' like this, before this last month?
I... no, not really. I don't remember anything like that. Just... normal, I guess. I haven't really noticed.
During these high-energy times, have you felt unusually confident, special, or like you could do things better than most people—more so than you normally would?
I don't... I wouldn't say that. I just... I feel good. Not really better than anyone else, just... capable, I guess. I haven't really thought about it like that.
Over this past month, have these upbeat, high-energy days been happening continuously, day after day without a break, or do they come and go with some days feeling more normal or low in between?
I guess... they just sort of happen. I haven't really been tracking it day by day. It's just... been a lot of energy lately. I don't know if it's every single day.
Over the past month, would you say you've felt this unusually upbeat and energetic on most days for at least a full week straight, or has it been more on-and-off than that?

I suppose... it's been most days. Some days I just feel really upbeat, you know? Like I have the energy to fix up the whole house and get everything done at work before dinner. But... I don't know, if my husband questions what I'm doing, I just... I might snap at him over something stupid. It just happens.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a ~1-month period of persistently elevated, expansive mood accompanied by increased energy, pressured/rapid speech, racing thoughts (flight of ideas), distractibility, increased goal-directed activity, and irritability. These symptoms have caused clear functional impairment (work errors requiring supervisor oversight, escalating marital conflict). No depressive or prior manic/hypomanic episodes were identified, ruling out Bipolar Disorder (F31.x) as this appears to be a single manic episode. Generalized anxiety and depressive disorders were explicitly denied. Grandiosity and decreased need for sleep were not endorsed, but the required threshold of ≥3 manic symptoms plus mood change with functional impairment is met, supporting a diagnosis of Manic Episode, unspecified (F30.9) given incomplete characterization of psychotic features.
